results.name: Plyo Side Lunge Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and both arms extended straight out to your sides.
Bend your right knee and lower into a side lunge while simultaneously rotating your torso to the right and bringing your left hand to touch your right leg. Keeping your left leg straight.
Push off your right foot to return to the starting wide stance position, straightening your right leg and rotating your torso back to the center.

Repeat the movement on the left side, bending your left knee into a side lunge and rotating your torso to bring your right hand to touch your left leg. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your bent knee stays aligned with your toes to avoid strain on your knee joint.
Move with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lower into the lunge and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Plyo Side Lunge Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Pretzel Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee, placing your right foot flat on the floor inside your left thigh.
Rotate your torso to the right and place your left elbow on the outside of your right knee, using your right hand on the floor behind you for support.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by switching the positions of your legs and rotating your torso to the left.
tips: Use your supporting hand on the floor behind you to maintain balance and assist with the rotation.
Move into the stretch slowly and with control to prevent overstretching and injury.
Breathe deeply and steadily, using your breath to help deepen the stretch and relax your muscles.
results.description: Pretzel Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your right arm, slightly bent, across your body at shoulder height.
Use your left hand to gently pull your right arm towards your chest, feeling the stretch in the rear deltoid.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by extending your left arm and using your right hand to assist with the stretch.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears to maximize the stretch.
Avoid twisting your torso; keep your upper body facing forward.
Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
results.description: Rear Deltoid Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch
instructions: Stand in the middle of a weight cage with a horizontal bar at chest level. Place the resistance band under your left foot and hold the other end of the band with your left hand.
Bring your left elbow up and rest it on the horizontal bar, allowing your forearm to lean backward. The band should extend down by your shoulder, creating tension.
Slowly allow your forearm to lean back to increase the stretch in your shoulder, keeping your hand close to your shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then slowly release the tension and switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your elbow securely on the bar to ensure proper stretch.
Allow your forearm to naturally lean back without forcing the movement.
Keep a relaxed grip on the band to avoid unnecessary tension.
results.description: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Revolved Head to Knee
instructions: Sit with one leg extended to the side and the other bent, foot against the inside of the extended thigh.
Turn your torso toward the bent knee.
Side-bend over the extended leg and reach your top arm overhead toward the foot.
Hold, breathing into the side of your body, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your chest open toward the ceiling.
Bend the extended knee slightly if your hamstrings are tight.
results.description: Revolved Head to Knee is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lats, Adductors.

results.name: Runner Stretch
instructions: Begin in a standing position with your feet hip-width apart.
Step your right foot slightly forward, keeping it straight. Lightly bend your left knee.
Lower your torso and arms towards your right foot, reaching down with your hands while keeping your back straight.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right hamstring. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
tips: Ensure your front knee remains straight but not locked to maximize the hamstring stretch.
Keep your back leg slightly bent and your heel on the floor to deepen the calf stretch.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and prevent slipping.
results.description: Runner Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Seated Calf Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Extend your right foot while lightly bending the left knee, reaching forward to grasp your toes with both hands.
Gently pull your toes towards you, feeling the stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release. Repeat on the left leg.
tips: Focus on maintaining a straight back to enhance the effectiveness of the stretch.
Ensure your movements are slow and controlled to prevent overstretching or injury.
If you find it difficult to reach your toes, use a towel or strap for assistance without forcing the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears to prevent unnecessary tension.
results.description: Seated Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

results.name: Seated Figure Four With Twist Glute Stretch
instructions: Sit tall with your legs extended.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and draw that foot in.
Twist your torso toward the bent knee, placing your opposite elbow against it.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Sit tall; don't round your back.
Breathe and deepen the twist slowly.
results.description: Seated Figure Four With Twist Glute Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Lower Back.

results.name: Seated Forward Bend
instructions: Sit with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Sit tall and inhale, reaching your arms up.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hips, reaching toward your feet.
Hold, breathing slowly.
tips: Lead with your chest, not your head.
Bend your knees if your hamstrings are tight.
results.description: Seated Forward Bend is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Calves.

results.name: Seated Side Bend Pose
instructions: Sit cross-legged with a tall spine.
Place one hand on the floor beside you.
Reach the other arm overhead and lean toward the hand on the floor.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep both hips on the floor.
Breathe into the side of your ribs.
results.description: Seated Side Bend Pose is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.
